extracted.intended_audience: researchers, engineers, companies, and institutions seeking DARPA DSO research or funding opportunities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and expectations for research programs and engagements under DARPA's Defense Sciences Office, emphasizing high-risk/high-payoff science that advances operational limits across specified thrust areas and moves from early ideas to prototype demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: DSO mission and portfolio focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Defense Sciences Office (DSO) works to identify and create the next generation of scientific discovery to fuel innovation throughout the Agency and beyond. DSO develops and manages an aggressive and forward-leaning portfolio that expands the art of the possible across a broad set of technical areas. By pushing science toward fundamental operational limits, our programs create a strategic advantage for the DOW. Our work is global in scale, as we monitor and drive the technological landscape and potential impacts on our military and our nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target foundational scientific advances that push toward fundamental operational limits and promise strategic advantage; portfolio emphasis is on aggressive, forward-leaning, high-risk/high-reward research with global awareness of technological trends and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of project maturity (scope from idea to prototype)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DSO portfolio ranges from early idea development and scientific validation to prototype demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSO supports work across stages — from nascent concepts and scientific validation through prototype demonstration — so proposals may be targeted at early exploratory work or at demonstrating practical prototypes; ensure stated objectives match the targeted maturity level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials, Manufacturing, and Energy Systems thrust
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking tensions between performance and efficiency for new materials, manufacturing flexibility, propulsion, and energy availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should aim to resolve trade-offs (e.g., performance vs. efficiency), enable flexible/manufacturable solutions, and address propulsion or energy availability challenges in ways that materially improve operational capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensing, Measuring, and Affecting thrust
rubrics_metrics.description: Bringing new science to overcome existing frontiers currently limiting the performance and/or practicality of sensing, measurement, and control, to achieve orders-of-magnitude improvement in operational capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate how new science or approaches will overcome current limits in sensing/measurement/control and justify claims of orders-of-magnitude improvements in operational metrics or practicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Math, Computation, and Processing thrust
rubrics_metrics.description: Enabling quantum, reimagining classical, and developing entirely new forms of computing for enhanced efficiency and new capabilities. Solutions may range from new approaches to hardware (implementation), algorithms (including representations), and computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should propose substantive advances in computational paradigms (quantum or novel classical) including hardware, algorithmic, and representational contributions that lead to new capabilities or efficiency gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex, Dynamic, and Intelligent Systems thrust
rubrics_metrics.description: Developing new methods, measures, and standards for a class of problems that elude our current approaches of study, analysis, and control. These are highly complex, dynamic, and often recursive systems that evolve over time and for which statistical methods fail. Applications range from dynamics of homeostatic systems to the foundations and emergence of intelligence for human-AI ecosystems, for the purposes and to enable warfighter capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should target problems where existing methods fall short (e.g., non-stationary, recursive, evolving systems), and offer new theoretical/measurement/control frameworks or standards that enable practical advances for defense-relevant complex systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of engagement and opportunity mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Opportunities to engage include R&D programs and efforts, challenge competitions, and technology transition efforts for the Defense Sciences Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider which engagement mechanism best fits their work (e.g., program funding vs. challenge competition vs. transition initiative) and tailor proposals to the expectations and evaluation modes of that mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program duration and expected impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Pushing Technology's Limits — Our DSO research programs are finite in duration, but the revolutionary advancements they drive create lasting change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be time-bounded with clear milestones and a credible plan to deliver revolutionary or lasting advances within the program lifetime; emphasize potential long-term impact despite finite funding duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program manager role and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: DSO program managers are visionary leaders whose experience spans industry, government, and academia. They conceive, plan, and oversee the high-risk R&D efforts for which we are best known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with program managers who typically shepherd high-risk programs; proposals and interactions should align with the PM's vision and the high-risk/high-payoff profile of DSO efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global technology awareness and strategic relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work is global in scale, as we monitor and drive the technological landscape and potential impacts on our military and our nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate awareness of the global technological landscape and articulate potential national/defense relevance and impacts, not only narrow technical novelty.
